## 3. filtlong installation

code to install filtlong

```{bash}
conda create -n filtlong_env -c bioconda filtlong
```

## 4. Run filtlong on yeast genome

filtlong bash tool is used to filter the long reads based on certain criteria such as average Q score

```{bash}
filtlong --keep_percent 75 data/ERR1539006.fastq.gz > outputs/filtlong_filtered_reads.fastq
```

## 5. Run sequali on filtered file

```{bash}
sequali outputs/filtlong_filtered_reads.fastq --outdir outputs
```

## 6. Description of how results changed after filtration
### Sanity check points prior filtration:
1. N50 is 8078 bp
2. From sequence length distribution, we can say that about 75% of reads are longer than 3499 bp. Thus, most reads are longer than 2000 bp
3. Read length histogram is unimodal (major peak around 5000 - 8000 bp) & broad (read lengths are widely distributed)
4. Average q score is less than 7, which means quality depletion. Only 22.71 % of reads have q score greater than 7, while 11.13 % of reads have q score greater than 10
5. From per position quality percentiles approximation, we can say that base quality levels remain stable around phred score of 30 with score dropping down to 20 beyond position 14000

### Sanity check points post filtration:
1. N50 is 8816 bp
2. From sequence length distribution, we can say almost all reads are longer than 2000 bp
3. Read length histogram is bimodal (two peaks: one around 6624 - 6691 bp while other around 8853 - 9290 bp)
4. Q score improved a little after filtration. Now, 36.42 % of reads have q score greater than 7, while 18.76 % of reads have q score greater than 10
5. From per position quality percentiles approximation, we can say that base quality levels remain stable around phred score of 30 with score dropping down to 20 beyond position 12000

Sequencing run is not of very good quality as average q score is less than 7. Also, we can not use it for the downstream analysis as it is required to trim the ends of reads before performing any downstream analysis on it.

## 8. Download the illumina reads of a Campilobacter jejuni genome sequencing 
To do so, run the following in R terminal
wget -nc -P data/ ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR112/040/ERR11203340/ERR11203340_1.fastq.gz
wget -nc -P data/ ftp://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR112/040/ERR11203340/ERR11203340_2.fastq.gz

## 9. R code chunk

rqc tool performs quality check on short read files

```{r}
qcres <- rqc(path = "data/", pattern = "^ERR11203340_.*\\.fastq\\.gz$", pair = c(1,1), openBrowser=FALSE, outdir="outputs")
```

## Sequencing quality per base/cycle

quality score drops below 2 at cycle 101

```{r}
rqcCycleQualityBoxPlot(qcres)
```

## Sequence content per base/cycle

Highest proportion for Ns is 0% because the line for N sits completely flat at the bottom of the graph across all the cycles

```{r}
rqcCycleBaseCallsLinePlot(qcres)
```

## Read frequency plot

Most of the sequences (about more than 40%) have 1 read, which means they are unique. Only small proportion of sequences are not unique.

```{r}
rqcReadFrequencyPlot(qcres)
```
